title: Hub survivors: which knot classes are rebuilt by hub gadgets of their own copies
claim: The 34 relations on three bits with every two coordinates unconstrained, other than the full cube, form 16 classes up to coordinate order. A hub gadget joins copies of one relation (any placements) with three legs in one copy each, hidden variables in at least two distinct copies, no variable twice in a copy, connected. Theorem 1: copies sharing one triple of variables intersect their placements; from twisted not-all-equal this reaches an equality on two coordinates, and from x or (y != z) and the three-excluded classes it reaches parity, while x or (y = z), not-all-equal and the no-lone-value classes reach neither. Theorem 2 (exhaustive over gadgets of at most six copies): the classes rebuilt are exactly the two parity classes, the two three-excluded classes with a symmetry of order two, twisted not-all-equal and the two x or (y != z) classes (smallest gadgets: three copies for parity, four for the others). Theorem 3: the two monotone atoms (excluding only 000, or only 111) are never rebuilt, at any size. Not-all-equal is rebuilt at seven copies (ticket B), so the census bounds, not decides, the remaining classes.
failure_conditions: A class rebuilt by a hub gadget of at most six copies other than those listed, or a listed class not rebuilt at its stated size.
A hub gadget with at least two copies rebuilding a monotone atom.
Parallel intersections of a class reaching parity or a two-coordinate equality other than as stated.
foundation_claim_scope: Set-level relations on three bits that pass K1-K3, in 16 classes up to coordinate order; hub gadgets as stated, exhaustive over three to six copies with every placement; the monotone-atom statement for every size; the remaining classes are bounded, not decided, since not-all-equal is rebuilt at seven copies.

validation.status: checked: 34 knots in 16 classes; intersection closures of every class (parity reached by x or (y != z) and the three-excluded classes, an equality by twisted not-all-equal, neither by the others); the fast enumeration equals a full canonical enumeration at 3, 4, 5 copies (3, 11, 104 shapes) and a size-first ordering misses shapes (control); exhaustive census of hub gadgets with 3 to 6 copies (1183 shapes, every placement): exactly seven classes rebuilt (parity from three copies, five others from four), the other nine not; monotone atoms never rebuilt (every copy holds a hidden variable); without hubs only parity is rebuilt; all-equal is rebuilt (control). The census bounds the nine classes, not decides them (not-all-equal is rebuilt at seven copies, ticket B); no human or external review
